$comment: Verified source registry for ShramSetu knowledge-base ingestion. Entries were fetched and read during the 2026-10-15 research pass, the 2026-10-30 curation pass and the 2026-11-03 phase-2 verification pass unless status says otherwise. Ingest only entries with status 'verified'. Entries with status 'unverified'/'superseded'/'uncertain' MUST NOT be served as trusted production answers.

status_values.verified: Fetched and read; content confirmed on the date given.
status_values.unverified: Claimed or referenced but the source content could not be read. Do not use as a citation.
status_values.superseded: Legally or factually replaced. Safe only as historical context, never as current law or current scheme status.
status_values.uncertain: Source readable but does not establish current status of the thing it describes.

entries.title: Code on Wages, 2019 — section 45 (claims) and 3-year limitation
entries.notes: Primary wage-claim route after the 21 Nov 2025 commencement. Replaces Payment of Wages Act 1936 route for post-commencement wage periods.

entries.title: Code on Wages, 2019 — section 17 (payment deadlines)
entries.notes: Timing only: end of shift (daily), before weekly holiday (weekly), 2nd day after fortnight (fortnightly), before 7th of following month (monthly); within 2 working days after removal/dismissal/retrenchment/resignation. NOT the wage-slip provision.

entries.title: Code on Wages, 2019 — section 50 (register of wages and wage slips)
entries.notes: s.50(1) register; s.50(3) wage slips. Exemption for employers of <=5 persons for agricultural or domestic purposes, who must produce reasonable proof of payment on demand.

entries.title: Code on Wages, 2019 — section 59 (burden of proof on employer)
entries.notes: For a claim alleging non-payment, underpayment or unauthorised deduction, the employer bears the burden of proving the dues were paid. High-value point for worker-facing guidance.

entries.title: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 — Rule 51 (registers, electronic or physical, 5-year retention)
entries.notes: Central-sector establishments only. State-sector (e.g. Kerala) rules must be confirmed separately.

entries.title: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026 — Rule 52 (wage slips in Form V, on or before payment)
entries.notes: Central-sector establishments only.

entries.title: PRS — Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026; commencement 21 November 2025
entries.notes: Central Rules finalized 8 May 2026; apply to central-sector establishments.

entries.title: FAOLEX/UNEP — Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (No. 37); entry into force 21 November 2025
entries.notes: Direct successor to the Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979. Repeal-and-savings at OSH Code s.143. Threshold: 10 or more inter-state migrant workers at an establishment on a day in the preceding 12 months. Definition now reaches some directly recruited and self-migrated workers.

entries.title: Inter-State Migrant Workmen (RE&CS) Act, 1979
entries.notes: REPEALED with effect from 21 November 2025. Historical context only. Its displacement allowance (50% of monthly wages or INR 75, whichever higher) has NO verified successor. Do not present as current law.

entries.title: Kerala Inter-State Migrant Workmen Rules, 1983 and the 2025 amendment
entries.notes: Listed on the Kerala Labour Commissionerate government-orders page, including a 2025 amendment, but the amendment PDF could not be read. Exact current fee table is NOT verified. Do not quote fees.

entries.title: Kerala Labour Commissionerate — 'What's new' (rules under the four Codes listed as Draft Rules)
entries.notes: Commencement of a Code is not the same as finalization of state rules. Kerala forms, fees and procedures may still change. Advise workers to confirm the current authority and form.

entries.title: Kerala Labour Commissionerate — Minimum Wage Notifications
entries.notes: There is NO single Kerala minimum wage. Rate depends on scheduled employment x classification/skill x area/zone x variable DA or later revision. Never hardcode a figure. Requires occupation, classification and location; direct to the latest FINAL notification plus subsequent revisions.

entries.title: Employer/project duties under BOCW and the Codes (cess, registration, worker eligibility)
entries.notes: Kerala Board states 1% of actual construction cost is levied from the employer as cess. Cess is an EMPLOYER/project liability and must never be presented as a worker deduction or fee. The familiar worker test (age 18-60, 90 days' construction work in preceding 12 months) is the OLD BOCW regime; Kerala's post-Code criteria were not verified.

entries.title: e-Shram FAQ (registration, eligibility, Aadhaar-linked mobile requirement)
entries.notes: Unorganised-sector home-based, self-employed or wage worker aged 16+, not an ESIC/EPFO member. Requires Aadhaar and an Aadhaar-linked mobile; without a linked mobile, a Common Service Centre or State Seva Kendra biometric route applies. Registration free; card does not expire. A UAN is NOT cash, insurance, a job or proof of scheme enrolment.

entries.title: ATHIDHI (Kerala) registration portal and app
entries.notes: Registration and administration system for migrant workers, employers and contractors. NOT a welfare scheme. A card is not proof of insurance, enrolment or benefit approval. No public third-party API found. Do NOT claim ATHIDHI registration activates AAWAZ cover. App listing verified; portal itself timed out on fetch.

entries.title: ATHIDHI registrations ~4.2 lakh as of 15 September 2025
entries.notes: Registration count, NOT a population headcount. Categories overlap. Never derive population shares from it.

entries.title: AAWAZ / Aawaaz health scheme — legacy benefits vs current status
entries.notes: Legacy page described INR 15,000/yr treatment and INR 2 lakh accidental-death cover, cashless via biometric card, ages 18-60. Reporting indicates enrolment CLOSED IN 2022 and researchers describe it as largely non-functional since 2019; only 347 of 5.16 lakh registrants had benefited as of 2023. Do NOT present cover as currently active. Confirm with the Labour Department before presenting any benefit as available.

entries.title: Mahatma Gandhi University study (Sep 2025) — very low health coverage among Kerala migrant workers
entries.notes: Only the article headline and URL slug were obtained; the page content was not read. The slug suggests '9.8%' but the exact figure is NOT verified. Cite the study's existence as reported, not a precise percentage.

entries.title: Inter-State Migrant Workers Welfare Scheme (ISMWWS, 2010, Kerala)
entries.notes: 2019-published terms: ages 18-60, enrol after one month in Kerala, renewable annual fee INR 30, benefits include death compensation, accident relief, treatment assistance, repatriation, education and maternity assistance (per a 2020 study). Registered terms are NOT confirmation that any benefit or amount is currently processed unchanged. 1.65 lakh registrations reported 2025. No public API found.

entries.title: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)
entries.notes: Portability of an EXISTING NFSA ration-card entitlement at a Fair Price Shop away from the card's home location, via ePoS biometric/Aadhaar authentication. Does NOT issue a ration card, does NOT create an entitlement, does NOT provide cash, does NOT guarantee stock. No public transaction API found.

entries.title: National Career Service (NCS) — helpline 1514
entries.notes: Job search, employer vacancy posting, job fairs, career centres, counsellors, training providers. Does NOT guarantee a job, placement, employer conduct, wages, visa or recruitment outcome. NCS warns about impersonators and states its services are free. No public job-search API found; scraped listings must never be presented as an official live feed.

entries.title: UMANG — onboarding is department-facing, not a public private-app API
entries.notes: UMANG presents services owned by their departments. Onboarding is via backend API integration by the government department/service provider. That is NOT evidence of a public API for private apps. Service pages returned only their JavaScript shell on fetch.

entries.title: CPGRAMS public grievance portal
entries.notes: Lodge a grievance, track the registration ID, give feedback and appeal when rated 'Poor'. Excludes RTI, sub judice, religious and most government-employee service matters. Not a court or guarantee of outcome. Official disclaimer permits direct deep links; a link is NOT an API grant. No public filing/retrieval API found. A generated draft is NOT a filed complaint.

entries.title: Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)
entries.notes: Statutory board for REGISTERED building and other construction workers. Benefits include pension/family and invalid pension, death and accident assistance, medical and maternity benefits, education assistance, marriage and funeral assistance, some loans. NOT a general migrant-worker registry. ATHIDHI card != board membership != AAWAZ != ONORC. No public third-party API found.

entries.title: eMigrate (MEA) — OVERSEAS employment only
entries.notes: For overseas employment/emigration: registered recruiting agents, emigrant registration, emigration clearance, complaints about agents. NOT for movement between Indian states. Do not use for interstate migration. Is not a guarantee a foreign offer is genuine.

entries.title: Kerala Labour Commissionerate — Register complaint; Labour Call Centre 1800 42555 214; Citizen Call Centre 155300
entries.notes: No public API found. '155214' is associated with the KARNATAKA labour helpline in search results and must NOT be listed as a Kerala number.

entries.title: Kerala CMO (Santhwanam) grievance channel — 1076
entries.notes: General state public-grievance channel, not migrant-specific. Track by docket number and registered mobile. ~15-day target for examination; complex cases take longer. No promised outcome.

entries.title: Samadhan — national labour grievance portal
entries.notes: Handles specified wage and employment complaints. World Bank notes it would need to include the interstate migrant-worker law to address migrant-specific vulnerabilities under the OLD framework.

entries.title: India Labourline — free legal aid and mediation for workers; 1-800-833-9020
entries.notes: NGO-run, not a government database. Its complaint statistics are the principal available wage-theft evidence for Kerala but are NOT an official state-wide count.

entries.title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 — electronic records (s.61, s.62, s.63, Schedule certificate; s.170 savings)
entries.notes: Replaced the Evidence Act from 1 July 2024. s.63 governs admissibility of computer output with a Schedule certificate (described as two-part: person in charge + expert, with device particulars and hash). Discussion relies on accessible legal commentary; the original judgment/statute PDFs were not retrieved. Applies to FORMAL JUDICIAL PROCEEDINGS; a labour authority or mediation may be less formal. Never auto-generate a certificate as if legally effective.

entries.title: Kerala — no official current survey of migrant worker numbers; ~31 lakh estimate (2021)
entries.notes: Labour Minister told the Assembly in 2025 that no official survey had established the current number. The ~31 lakh figure is a 2021 estimate. Registration counts (5.16L Aawaaz, 4.2L ATHIDHI, 1.65L ISMWWS) overlap and are not a headcount. Never present a definitive population figure.

entries.title: India Labourline wage-theft complaints: ~1,152-1,227 cases, ~INR 2.4 crore, 16-18 months
entries.notes: Reporting cut-offs differ (Feb 2024 vs May 2024); totals must NOT be summed into one dataset. ~9 in 10 complaints concerned pending wages; 85%+ construction. Recovery ~INR 51-55 lakh. This is complaint data from one NGO channel, NOT prevalence and NOT an official state-wide count.

entries.title: Supreme Court order, In Re: Problems and Miseries of Migrant Labourers (20 April 2023)
entries.notes: ~28.60 crore e-Shram registrations, of which ~20.63 crore also appeared in ration-card data. The Court said those without ration-card registration might be deprived of NFSA benefits and directed states/UTs to issue cards to eligible workers. The 28.60 crore figure is NOT a count of interstate migrant workers.

entries.title: AI4Bharat IndicTrans2 translation model
entries.notes: Model checkpoints MIT-licensed. Covers Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Odia, Assamese, Maithili and other scheduled languages. DOES NOT LIST BHOJPURI. Self-hostable (Fairseq / Hugging Face / CTranslate2); no guaranteed minimum hardware spec. Dataset licences differ (CC0 and CC-BY-4.0) - check per artifact.

entries.title: Meta NLLB-200 (includes Bhojpuri and Maithili) - NOT production-usable
entries.notes: LICENCE CC-BY-NC 4.0. Model card states it is a RESEARCH model, not released for production deployment, NOT intended for legal or other domain-specific text or document translation, and cannot provide certified translations. DO NOT use as a production Bhojpuri fallback.

entries.title: Bhashini / ULCA hosted language API - PoC-only public terms
entries.notes: Public API docs state use is FOR PROOF OF CONCEPT ONLY; production or paid-user use should contact Bhashini for its paid version. No published production price, guaranteed free quota or rate limits found. Onboarding requires DIBD approval for userID/keys; per-call flow is pipeline-config then pipeline-compute using the returned callbackURL and inference-key header. Credentials must stay server-side. Confirm data-retention and liability terms before sending worker legal/health/wage data.

entries.title: AI4Bharat IndicConformer ASR (MIT)
entries.notes: MIT-licensed monolingual checkpoints for Assamese, Bengali, Hindi, Maithili, Malayalam, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, plus a multilingual 600M model. Uses AI4Bharat's NeMo fork. NO Bhojpuri checkpoint.

entries.title: Vistaar / IndicWhisper benchmark WER per language
entries.notes: Average WER: Hindi 13.6%, Bengali 20.1%, Tamil 25.3%, Odia 27.4%, Telugu 28.8%, Malayalam 32.3%. Lowest WER on 39 of 59 benchmarks. No comparable figures for Assamese, Maithili or Bhojpuri. Benchmark results, NOT a guarantee for any worker, district, microphone or conversation.

entries.title: Sruti study (2025) - Bhojpuri ASR baseline 33.3% WER vs Hindi 15%
entries.notes: Only 23 transcribed Bhojpuri hours in Vaani; major collection/transcription barriers. Domain: health, agriculture, governance, finance for rural Bhojpuri-speaking women. Must inform refusal and read-back behaviour for Bhojpuri.

entries.title: Unadapted Whisper baseline WER on Indian languages (Kathbath)
entries.notes: Reported WER: Hindi 42.64, Bengali 134.98, Tamil 63.90, Malayalam 134.40. Fine-tuning improved results substantially but used four A100 GPUs. 'Whisper supports the language' is NOT evidence of fitness.

entries.title: Indic Parler-TTS metadata
entries.notes: Apache 2.0, 0.94B params, ~3.75 GB, gated: auto, inference: false - downloadable but NOT a turnkey hosted API. Language tags DO NOT list Bhojpuri or Maithili.

entries.title: WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference
entries.notes: Text alternatives required for non-text content; accessible names for controls. Never make an icon the only explanation of a control.

entries.title: NN/g research on mobile behaviour in India (shared phones, app locks, accidental disclosure)
entries.notes: Small qualitative studies (incl. 2016, 10 participants) - use as a design signal, NOT a current prevalence estimate. Supports: ephemeral sessions, app lockers/PINs, and risk of disclosure via notifications and visible phone content.

entries.title: Android Private Space - availability limits
entries.notes: Requires Android 15 or later and supported hardware; cannot be used as a guest or secondary-user space. An optional user facility, NOT a safe baseline for the app.

entries.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment nationwide heatwave advisory to States/UTs (28 April 2026)
entries.notes: Advisory-only (non-binding guidance to States/UTs and attached organisations): flexibility/slower pace in extreme heat, two-person crews where continuous work is unavoidable, rest areas with ventilation/cooling, special attention to construction, brick-kiln, daily-wage and casual workers, awareness campaigns at labour chowks. NOT a cash benefit and NOT an enforceable rule.

entries.title: KPMG summary — final Central Rules under the four Labour Codes notified 8 May 2026
entries.notes: Secondary summary; the underlying Gazette notifications were not read directly. Reports: Grievance Redressal Committee mandatory for industrial establishments with 20+ workers (max 20 members; worker representatives not fewer than employer representatives); contract-labour grievances on wages, health or working conditions addressed by the principal employer through a committee, escalating to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator if unresolved within 30 days. Codes in force 21 November 2025. Central-sector rules only — state rules may still be drafts; do not quote state-specific forms or fees.

entries.title: News Minute (2022) — AAWAZ uptake: ~374 of ~5.16 lakh cardholders received medical help over ~4 years
entries.notes: Awareness-failure evidence: card seen as work ID, empanelled hospitals and claim steps unknown, outreach mostly Malayalam/English rather than workers' own languages. Enrolment reportedly closed 2022; scheme described as largely non-functional in recent years. NEVER present AAWAZ cover as currently active (pair with aawaz-status entry).

entries.title: UNFPA–IIMAD South India Interstate Migration Survey (SIIMS 2026) — 1,824 workers across KA/KL/TN
entries.notes: Survey (not prevalence) across 33 districts: 86.4% no signed employment contract, 57.6% paid in cash, 77.4% recruited via non-contractor channels, 73.3% problems accessing welfare, 69.2% trouble with healthcare. Average monthly wage Rs 17,640; average working day 9.87 hours. Read with category-specific caution; do not present as Kerala-only figures.

entries.title: PIB press release PRID 2192463 — four Labour Codes effective 21 November 2025
entries.notes: The commencement release the current/superseded corpus headers cite. pib.gov.in returned 403 to automated fetch on 2026-10-20; the 21 Nov 2025 commencement date is independently corroborated (KPMG alert 2026-007, DLA Piper) and matches every dated repo document. Registrar entry exists so the loader gate passes the four current-Code documents; source pages themselves were exercised via registry-approved secondary reporting.

entries.title: PIB press release PRID 2193095 — Code on Wages, 2019 (laws subsumed: Minimum Wages 1948, Payment of Wages 1936, Bonus 1965, Equal Remuneration 1976)
entries.notes: Same 403 caveat as pib-codes-commencement: automated fetch blocked, content corroborated through the repo's Code on Wages documents and secondary legal reporting. Gate entry so code-on-wages-2019.txt and unpaid-wage-remedies-code-on-wages-2019.txt load.

entries.title: Department of Food and Public Distribution — portal (Toll Free 1967)
entries.notes: Fetched 2026-10-30; header confirms 'Toll Free Number: 1967'. Search-result render of the same portal also lists Anna Sahayata IVRS 14457 and WhatsApp 9868200445. A national ONORC helpline 14445 is listed by SOME state food departments (e.g. Maharashtra) — confirm per state before quoting.

entries.title: PMGKAY — free foodgrains for NFSA beneficiaries, 5 years from 1 Jan 2024
entries.notes: The DFPM PMGKAY page is a JS shell to automated fetch. Content verified through PIB releases PRID 1980686 and PRID 2086345: free foodgrains to 81.35 crore NFSA beneficiaries (AAY 35 kg/family, priority households 5 kg/person) for five years effective 1 Jan 2024 (to 31 Dec 2028). The earlier separate COVID-era PMGKY add-ons (e.g. 1 kg pulses per person for migrants) are NOT part of the current regime. DFPD page facts re-checked 2026-10-30.

entries.title: PIB release PRID 2192802 — Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 highlights
entries.notes: Release (22 Nov 2025) on the OSH Code: no employee to work more than 8 hours a day / 48 hours a week; inter-state migrant provisions highlighted. pib.gov.in returned 403 to automated fetch on 2026-10-30; 8h/48h corroborated by the labour.gov.in OSH FAQ PDF and overtime-at-twice-rates by the DG FASLI Code PDF (both registered). The coverage text is a summary — consult the Code text for exact s. references.

entries.title: DG FASLI official OSH Code PDF — overtime at twice the rate
entries.notes: Government DG FASLI publication of the OSH Code text: wages at twice the rate for overtime work. Also relevant for hours/rest-interval structure.

entries.title: Ministry of Labour & Employment FAQ PDF on the OSH Code (uploaded Jan 2026)
entries.notes: Official FAQ: 8 hours/day and 48 hours/week standard, with consent-based extension of daily hours on premium payment. Use for the hours standard rather than quoting section numbers.

entries.title: EPFO official PDF — present rates of contribution (12% each side; EPS/EPF split)
entries.notes: Official EPFO PDF: employer contribution 12% split as EPS 8.33% and the remainder to EPF; contributions payable up to a wage ceiling of Rs 15,000 in this PDF's text. The statutory ceiling was later raised to Rs 25,000 by w.e.f. 17 Sep 2026 (see epfo-wage-ceiling-2026) — do not quote Rs 15,000 as the current ceiling.

entries.title: EPFO statutory wage ceiling raised to Rs 25,000/month effective 17 Sep 2026
entries.notes: Multiple consistent reports (KPMG flash alert 2026-253 FAQ; analyst/bank explainers) date the mandatory-coverage ceiling increase from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 at 17 Sep 2026. Gazette text not read directly; do not derive EPS-cap arithmetic without checking the gazette.

entries.title: EPF interest 8.25% for FY 2024-25 (ratified); retained at 8.25% for FY 2025-26 per reports
entries.notes: News Service/DD News: 8.25% ratified for FY 2024-25 (mid-2025). FY 2025-26 retention of 8.25% was announced around March 2026 and ratified June 2026 (news reports). Rates change annually — quote a rate only with its financial year.

entries.title: PMJJBY/PMSBY terms — premiums Rs 436 / Rs 20 w.e.f. 1 Jun 2022, still current for 2025-26
entries.notes: PIB release PRID 1823754 (May 2022) describes both schemes (covers Rs 2 lakh); premiums were Rs 330/Rs 12 at that date and were revised to Rs 436/Rs 20 effective 1 Jun 2022 (Finance-ministry-adjacent press; consistent across sources). Policy-year 2025-26 premiums remain Rs 436/Rs 20 (participating-bank communications). PMJJBY: any-cause death, ages 18-50, savings account + auto-debit. PMSBY: accidental death/total disability Rs 2 lakh, partial disability Rs 1 lakh, ages 18-70 (NOT 10-70 — fix any older text). PMSBY is accident-only; PMJJBY covers natural death; they are separate policies.

entries.title: PM-KISAN portal — Rs 6,000/yr in three Rs 2,000 DBT instalments; helpline 155261
entries.notes: pmkisan.gov.in did not load on automated fetch 2026-10-30. Core terms corroborated via multiple secondary write-ups (2021–22 era and later): income support Rs 6,000/year in three 4-monthly Rs 2,000 instalments via DBT; open to all landholding farmer families after the 2019 expansion (the earlier 'small and marginal only' cap is outdated); exclusions include institutional landholders, constitutional post-holders, serving/retired employees above notified pension levels, income-tax payers, professionals; helpline 155261. Benefit tied to landholding + separate bank accounts; not an entitlement for a landless migrant worker.

entries.title: Maandhan PM-SYM page — contribution chart, eligibility, family pension
entries.notes: Fetched 2026-10-30: entry age 18–40; monthly income up to Rs 15,000; member contribution Rs 55 (age 18) rising to Rs 200 (age 40) matched equally by GoI; assured pension Rs 3,000/month from 60; family pension = 50% (Rs 1,500) to the spouse only; must NOT be an EPFO/NPS/ESIC member or an income-tax payer; Aadhaar + savings/Jan-Dhan account with IFSC; enrolment via CSC. Content pages themselves carry last-updated dates around Feb 2023 — treat figures as 'as published on the portal'.

entries.title: NPS for Traders (Laghu Vyapari) on the Maandhan portal
entries.notes: Maandhan portal homepage (fetched 2026-10-30): National Pension Scheme for Traders — old-age protection for self-employed shop owners/retail traders; entry age 18–40; annual turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore; assured pension Rs 3,000/month from 60; GoI matching contribution.

entries.title: Ayushman Vay Vandana — all citizens 70+ covered with Rs 5 lakh/year PM-JAY
entries.notes: PM-JAY is Rs 5 lakh per family per year for eligible families; since the 29 Oct 2024 announcement, ALL citizens aged 70 and above are eligible regardless of income (Ayushman Vay Vandana). The Oct 2026 PIB piece (PRID 2330009) marks two years of the programme. General PM-JAY eligibility for younger families still depends on scheme criteria (SECC/NFSA-linked lists; check mera.pmjay.gov.in). Products/hospital counts change — avoid hard counts.

entries.title: PM-JAY support — helpline 14555 / 1800-111-565 (official support portal)
entries.notes: support.pmjay.gov.in lists 'Helpline No. 14555' and tech helpline 14555 / 1800111565 (also confirmed in an AIIMS patient booklet and the PM-JAY quality-certification site). Use both numbers; mera.pmjay.gov.in is the citizen eligibility portal.

entries.title: NSAP pension amounts (Nov 2025 PIB explainer + myScheme)
entries.notes: PIB (PRID 2187327, 7 Nov 2025) and myScheme: IGNOAPS central assistance Rs 200/month (60–79) and Rs 500 (80+); IGNWPS (widows 40+) and IGNDPS (severe disability) Rs 300/month with Rs 500 at 80+; NFBS one-time Rs 20,000 on breadwinner death; Annapurna = 10 kg foodgrains/month for uncovered eligible seniors. States add top-ups — naming state amounts requires local verification. BPL-based; application via panchayat/municipality; helpline numbers vary — use ministry portals.

entries.title: MGNREGA official FAQ PDF (NREGA Plus archive) — guarantee structure
entries.notes: Official NIC-archived MGNREGA FAQ: at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer; job card/demand-for-work/unemployment-allowance framework. Wage rates are notified by MoRD per state (do NOT equate with the state's agricultural minimum wage). Helpline number policy: verify per state — the 1800-180-5678 number seen in old material is NOT confirmed.

entries.title: MGNREGA guidelines for timely payment of wages (MoRD-hosted PDF, uploaded Jan 2025)
entries.notes: Official MoRD-hosted guidelines: wage payment within 15 days of closure of the muster roll; delay compensation at 0.05% of unpaid wages per day of delay beyond the sixteenth day. Wages go to bank/post-office accounts.

entries.title: PMKVY 4.0 guidelines (MSDE official PDF)
entries.notes: Official MSDE PMKVY 4.0 guidelines: short-term training/upskilling with training centres onboarded on Skill India Digital; RPL (Recognition of Prior Learning) for experienced workers. Skill India Digital PMKVY landing lists the 15–45 age band. Do NOT promise a fixed stipend or a fixed helpline number; enrolment windows are phased — check Skill India Digital for the current phase.

entries.title: PIB PRID 2297203 — PMKVY 4.0 course redesign (implemented since FY 2022-23)
entries.notes: PIB explainer: PMKVY 4.0 under implementation since FY 2022-23 with focus on emerging/new-age courses (AI etc.). Use as corroboration for the programme's current form; pib.gov.in 403 caveat as elsewhere.

entries.title: Atal Pension Yojana — government co-contribution ended (joined before 31 Mar 2016, FY 2015-16..2019-20)
entries.notes: Official FAQs (PFRDA; DFS pages; jansuraksha APY FAQ): GoI co-contribution applies ONLY to subscribers who joined before 31 Mar 2016 and only for FY 2015-16 through 2019-20. Never present APY as carrying a current government co-contribution. Guaranteed pension Rs 1,000–5,000/month from 60 for eligible subscribers aged 18–40.

entries.title: Budget 2025-26 (1 Feb 2025) — ID cards, e-Shram registration and PM-JAY healthcare for gig/platform workers
entries.notes: Consistent multi-outlet reporting of the Budget speech: identity cards, registration on e-Shram and healthcare under PM-JAY for gig/platform workers, plus a social-security scheme. Speech PDF itself returned 403; treat as budget-speech announcement with implementation details still rolling out — check labour.gov.in/NHA before promising delivery.

entries.title: PM SVANidhi 2.0 — Cabinet 27 Aug 2025: extended to 31 Mar 2030; tranches Rs 15k/Rs 25k/Rs 50k
entries.notes: Multiple outlets concur on the Cabinet decision: outlay Rs 7,332 crore; run-up to 31 Mar 2030; 1.15 crore beneficiaries including ~50 lakh new; first tranche up to Rs 15,000 (from Rs 10,000), second up to Rs 25,000 (from Rs 20,000), third up to Rs 50,000; UPI-linked RuPay credit cards; 7% interest-subsidy design continues per scheme history. Secondary reporting — the Gazette text was not read; verify final terms at pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in.

entries.title: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 — full text
entries.notes: PRS-hosted full Act text: Town Vending Committees; survey + certificate of vending; s.3 — no eviction or relocation until the survey is completed and the certificate issued. Not superseded by the Labour Codes (separate livelihood law). Penalty amounts (e.g. for vending without a certificate) are in the Act text and state rules — read the text before quoting a figure; do not quote 'Rs 2,000' from summaries.

entries.title: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 — NHRC-compiled text
entries.notes: NHRC's official compilation includes the Act text: system abolished; advances/compulsion punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine; vigilance committees at state and district level for identification, release and rehabilitation. Rehabilitation assistance is delivered through central/state schemes with changing names and amounts — do not restate old amounts without a current source.

entries.title: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 — PENCIL portal PDF
entries.notes: Official PENCIL portal hosts the amended Act text: no child below 14 in any occupation; adolescents (14–18) barred from hazardous occupations/processes; offence cognizable; penalties per the Act (read the text; commonly cited first-offence range imprisonment 6 months–2 years or fine Rs 20,000–50,000 — reconcile with the PDF before quoting outside structured outputs). Family-enterprise exception for children in non-hazardous, after-school work is narrow and regulated; state rules add conditions.

entries.title: Karnataka Labour Dept — child labour penalties summary (first offence Rs 20,000–50,000 etc.)
entries.notes: State government page: employing a child may attract imprisonment/fine, first offence Rs 20,000–50,000; repeat offence imprisonment 1–3 years. Useful as a real-world admin summary of the national Act; confirm current state norms before quoting.

entries.title: POSH Act, 2013 — full Act PDF hosted by the Department of Expenditure (Act 14 of 2013)
entries.notes: Government-hosted full text: ICC required for workplaces with 10+ employees; Local Committee via the District Officer for <10 employees / complaints against the employer itself; definition of sexual harassment; s.26 penalties start at up to Rs 50,000 and escalate (double penalty / licence cancellation on repeat); complaint window 3 months (with reasons-plus-3-months extension). Removes 'Employers with 50+ women workers must provide...' style elaborations unless they exist in the text.

entries.title: National Commission for Women — 24/7 helpline 7827-170-170 (+ Women Helpline 181)
entries.notes: NCW's own communications publish 7827170170 as the 24/7 helpline for women facing violence; the WCD 'Women Helpline' 181 continues. Complaints can also be filed digitally via NCW's system.

entries.title: PMAY-G unit assistance: Rs 1.20 lakh plain / Rs 1.30 lakh NER & hilly (incl. J&K, Ladakh) — PIB
entries.notes: PIB release 'Expansion of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin' (PRID 2113748): unit assistance Rs 1.20 lakh (plain areas) and Rs 1.30 lakh (NE states and hilly states incl. J&K and Ladakh). States have publicly sought an increase (reported Jan 2025) — confirm the current notified figure before pinning a number. Toilet-construction support (~Rs 12,000) flows via SBM-IHHL; verify locally.

entries.title: ESIC contribution rates (official portal page)
entries.notes: Fetched 2026-11-03. Since 1 July 2019: employer contributes 3.25% and employee 0.75% of wages. Employees with wages up to Rs 21,000/month are covered (Rs 25,000 for persons with disability). A wage up to Rs 176 per day exempts only the EMPLOYEE share — the employer contribution stays payable. Contribution periods: 1 April-30 September and 1 October-31 March; contributions payable within 15 days of the end of the month.
